items.title: Houthi strikes hit Riyadh airport again as Saudi Arabia probes air-defence failure
items.summary: Gulf News reports a fresh Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport that killed one Pakistani national and wounded 11. Saudi Arabia has opened an investigation into how its air defences failed to intercept the missile and drone barrage, and Riyadh schools have again moved to distance learning. CBS News adds that the attacks keep the airport closed while President Trump weighs U.S. strikes in Yemen.
items.why: Gulf airspace closures and escalation risk feed into fuel prices, airline costs and the Gulf-linked hiring and remittances many Indian families depend on.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz tension: Iran's navy claims a third tanker hit, crude near $103 to $107
items.summary: Just Security's early edition reports Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy claimed to have struck a third supertanker in the Strait of Hormuz, and its chief warned foreign powers against interfering in the Gulf. Brent crude is quoted at roughly $103 to $107 a barrel depending on the source, so treat the price as provisional. Iran's Mohsen Rezaei called the U.S. response to Iran's conditions for reopening the strait insufficient.
items.why: Oil is the transmission channel to Indian inflation, the rupee and company margins, and shipping risk is a live supply-chain case study.

items.title: Trump's energy ceasefire for Russia and Ukraine has no sign of Russian agreement
items.summary: Reports say Russian attacks killed at least six civilians on Sunday, including a strike on a grocery store in Kharkiv. There is no evidence Russia has agreed to the energy ceasefire President Trump announced. Ukrainian drones reportedly hit a Yandex data centre, and Zelenskyy said he would hold an election if Russia accepted a 60-day ceasefire.
items.why: A gap between an announcement and reality is a live lesson in credibility and crisis communication, and energy headlines move prices.

items.title: Six states get new governors
items.summary: Amar Ujala's headline roundup for 13 October reports that the President announced governor appointments for six states on Monday, including Kerala and Tamil Nadu, with Uttarakhand also getting a new governor. The source text is partial, so the full list is provisional.
items.why: Governor appointments shape centre-state dynamics, which matters for policy, investment climate and public-sector hiring.

items.title: INDIA bloc puts eight demands before the Supreme Court on the SIR voter-roll exercise
items.summary: Prabhat Khabar's morning top-20 list leads with the opposition INDIA bloc placing eight demands before the Supreme Court, including an interim stay on the SIR voter-roll exercise and a bar on removing names from voter lists. The same list mentions a petition concerning the Chief Election Commissioner. This is headline-level reporting from one source.
items.why: Electoral-roll rules affect who can vote, and this is a case study in how institutions communicate under public scrutiny.

items.title: Sensex and Nifty tumble on oil spike, rate-hike worries and foreign selling
items.summary: The Sensex fell nearly 548 points to close at 71,924.68 and the Nifty lost 157.10 points, or 0.70 per cent, to 22,363.35 on Monday, according to a 13 October report. Reports cite rate-hike worries, higher crude and persistent foreign fund outflows. Tuesday's session is not yet covered.
items.why: Market swings shape campus placement budgets, fintech and banking hiring sentiment, and the cost of capital for the firms recruiting you.

items.title: RBI rate hike and a tighter CRR rattle banks while retail inflation climbs to 5.54%
items.summary: The Week's analysis describes a rate shock after the RBI's hawkish stance, followed by a rebound that ended an eight-week losing streak, and an effort to protect the rupee. Banking stocks fell after the central bank raised the daily CRR maintenance requirement to absorb surplus liquidity, and retail inflation rose to 5.54 per cent in September, per other reports. Figures come from several outlets and should be treated as provisional.
items.why: Rate and inflation moves feed straight into consumer demand, pricing decisions and hiring plans, which are core inputs for marketing and HR roles.

items.title: Fact: retail inflation was 5.54% in September
items.summary: India's retail inflation rose to 5.54 per cent in September, according to reports around the 12 October market close.
items.why: A useful anchor figure for pricing, wage and cost-of-living discussions in class cases.

items.title: Microsoft unveils Maia 300, its next in-house AI chip, to lean less on Nvidia
items.summary: GeekWire reports Microsoft says its homegrown Maia chips will handle most of the AI work behind Copilot and its other products, with the new Maia 300 rolling out in 2027. Microsoft says it does more AI work per unit of electricity than the GPU systems that power most AI today.
items.why: Custom silicon changes the economics and competition of AI services, which affects the vendor and talent landscape you will recruit into.

items.title: Report: Nvidia plans to buy Hugging Face for about $13 billion
items.summary: Inc. reports, citing unconfirmed sources, that Nvidia is planning to acquire Hugging Face in a deal described as worth $13 billion. This is a report, not a confirmed deal, and the date of the original report is about two days old.
items.why: If confirmed, it would reshape who controls open AI tooling, a useful case for M&A and platform strategy discussions.

items.title: Fact: the rupee's hedging rush hit a record $77 billion
items.summary: A report says the rupee was set for a 1 per cent rally after the RBI curbed a hedging rush that had reached a record $77 billion. Provisional, from a single report.
items.why: Currency volatility affects import costs and the pricing of anything with foreign inputs.
